## Does the extension edit the IPYNB JSON directly?

No. It uses the VS Code Notebook API and edits notebook cells through the
active notebook editor.

## Which imports are moved?

Only top-level Python imports are collected. Parenthesized multi-line imports
are supported. Imports nested inside `TYPE_CHECKING`, `if`, `try`, functions,
and classes remain in their original location.

## Does Ruff have to be installed?

No. Ruff sorting is disabled by default. The built-in collection and
deduplication behavior does not depend on Python tools.

## What happens when Ruff is enabled but missing?

The normal organization still completes and the original import order is kept.
The extension records the Ruff error in its VS Code output channel.

## Can I use Ruff from a virtual environment?

Yes. Set `notebook-cell-organizer.ruff.command` to the absolute Ruff executable
path, or configure `uv` as described in the [Ruff setup guide](ruff.qmd).

## Can organization run automatically?

Yes. Enable `notebook-cell-organizer.organizeOnSave` in VS Code settings.

## How do I report an issue?

Open an issue in the
[GitHub repository](https://github.com/showpiecep/notebook-cell-organizer/issues)
with a minimal notebook example and the expected result.
